| Rank | Country | Area (km²) | Head‑of‑government title (2025) | Does the country have a **Prime Minister**? |

| **Tuvalu** | **Kausea Natano** (in office since 2019) | **Tuvaluan** (a Polynesian language). English is also an official language and Natano is fluent in it, but his mother‑tongue is Tuvaluan. |
| San Marino | *No prime minister* (head of government is the Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs) | – |

### Quick language note for the other four states  

Even though they do not have a prime minister, the heads of government in the other four tiny states are native speakers of the following languages:

| Country | Head of government (2025) | Native language(s) |
|---------|---------------------------|--------------------|
| Vatican City | Cardinal Secretary of State **Pietro Parolin** | Italian (native), Latin (ecclesiastical) |
| Monaco | Minister of State **Pierre Dartout** | French (native) |
| Nauru | President **David Adeang** | Nauruan (native) – also fluent in English |
| San Marino | Captains Regent **Michele Muratori & Lorenzo Cavalli** (2025‑2026 term) & Secretary of State **Luca Boschi** | Italian (native) |

### Bottom line
- **Only Tuvalu has a prime minister among the five smallest countries.**  
- The native language of that prime minister, **Kausea Natano**, is **Tuvaluan** (with English as a second official language).
